title: Kahana vs Nebula: When Reach Is Not the Whole Job
excerpt: Nebula is long-form video hosting, reach, and subscriptions. Kahana is the club layer and discovery signal for learning from video.
defaultImageQuery: Nebula The club layer and discovery signal for learning from video.
seoTitle: Kahana vs Nebula | When Reach Is Not the Whole Job

columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: Launched June 2019 by Standard and a collective of ~100 YouTube creators as a premium, ad-free companion to YouTube.
100k paying subscribers after year one; 600k+ by late 2022; 2023 started ~650k and ended ~680k with nearly 200k new direct subscribers and +162% direct MRR.
Early pricing ~USD 3/mo or USD 30/year; later often ~USD 5/mo, frequently bundled via creator sponsorships.
Early content pace ~250 new videos/month; 5,000+ videos within the first year.

strengths.title: Creator-owned, ad-free environment
strengths.detail: Built and owned by creators; ad-free viewing with long-form, essay-style, and experimental content.

strengths.title: Curated roster of quality creators
strengths.detail: Strong educational, commentary, and video-essay roster, good fit for knowledge clubs.

strengths.title: Exclusive and extended content
strengths.detail: Nebula-exclusive videos, extended cuts, series, and early releases often not on YouTube.

strengths.title: Stable subscription revenue
strengths.detail: More predictable income than YouTube ad volatility; operators emphasize MRR growth and lower churn.

weaknesses.title: Smaller catalog and brand awareness
weaknesses.detail: Far smaller than YouTube or Netflix, users usually find Nebula via creator sponsorships.

weaknesses.title: Limited categories (creator-essay heavy)
weaknesses.detail: Less breadth in mainstream series, movies, or kids’ programming.

weaknesses.title: Reliance on YouTube ecosystem for acquisition
weaknesses.detail: Growth depends heavily on creators promoting Nebula from YouTube channels and sponsorship slots.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. Nebula is long-form video hosting, reach, and subscriptions. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

Nebula is a creator-owned subscription video platform positioned as a ‘thoughtful expansion pack for YouTube,’ offering ad-free, exclusive content from a curated group of independent creators.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and Nebula side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On Nebula you can use Long-form video and Memberships as first-class product jobs. You need distribution, search, ads, or a native player at platform scale.

Using Kahana with Nebula

You can use both. Nebula keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep hosting and distribution on Nebula. Put the lectures or series that deserve a shelf into Kahana hubs, ideally via embed, then discuss them in a Club. Reach stays on Nebula; Kahana is where the work is findable after the tab is closed, and where you can grow an audience around it.
